College at the University of Vermont
The George D. Aiken Center houses the Rubenstein School of Environment and Natural Resources
The Rubenstein School of Environment and Natural Resources (RSENR) (established in 2003) is the University of Vermont's natural resources college. The University of Vermont recognized the importance of providing educational opportunities in this field of study, initiating forestry courses in 1888. The first school, originally called The School of Natural Resources was established in 1973.[1] The main home of the Rubenstein School of Environment and Natural Resources, the George D. Aiken Center opened in 1982. The building's name honors Vermont's distinguished late senator and governor.[2]
RSENR is home to a natural resources and field study based curriculum, has its own core courses and building. There are several majors including environmental sciences; fores

try; parks, recreation, and tourism; sustainability, ecology, and policy; and wildlife and fisheries biology.[1]
The Rubenstein School campus includes members of the UVM Environmental Program, the Gund Institute for Ecological Economics, the Rubenstein Ecosystem Science Laboratory, and the US Forest Service Northern Research Station.[3]
In 2012, the Aiken building housing the school was completely reconstructed as a green renovated facility and named the Aiken Center with a U.S. Green Building Council LEED certification of platinum, and has the highest certification score in the entire state of Vermont.[2] One of the other facilities belonging to the school is the Rubenstein Ecosystem Research Lab at the Burlington waterfront.

value.text:
The Rubenstein School of Environment and Natural Resources is the University of Vermont’s natural resources college in the United States. It forms part of the university rather than constituting a separate university. Its curriculum emphasizes natural resources and field study, with its own core courses. The subjects listed for its majors include environmental sciences; forestry; parks, recreation, and tourism; sustainability, ecology, and policy; and wildlife and fisheries biology.

The university’s teaching in this field extends back to forestry courses initiated in 1888. The original School of Natural Resources was established in 1973, while the Rubenstein School is described as established in 2003. These dates represent distinct stages in its development. Its principal home is the George D. Aiken Center, which opened in 1982 and was named in honor of Vermont senator and governor George D. Aiken. In 2012 the building underwent reconstruction as a green renovated facility and received LEED platinum certification. Another school facility is the Rubenstein Ecosystem Research Lab on the Burlington waterfront. The school’s campus also includes members of the university’s Environmental Program, the Gund Institute for Ecological Economics and the US Forest Service Northern Research Station.
